The original source code of Dead-Fest was stored exclusively on a single Hard Disk Drive (HDD) that suffered catastrophic hardware failure.
All legacy project archives, version histories, and uncommitted modules were permanently lost to the wasteland static.
Rather than abandoning the survivors, Dead-Fest was rebuilt entirely from scratch, engineering a more resilient, scalable, and powerful core architecture.
Crafted with modern UI components, sleek surfaces, high-contrast typography, and signature crimson atmospheric accents.
Rebuilt with strict reactive state management to eliminate memory leaks and runtime crashes under heavy network load.
Redesigned navigation flows and touch targets optimized for high-stress tactical environments and quick operator decisions.
Cuts transitions and speeds up the wheel on older, battered wasteland hardware. Switches on automatically for low-RAM devices (Settings → System).
Live data feeds disconnect a few seconds after the terminal is backgrounded and reconnect instantly on return.
Bypasses unnecessary initialization checks to drop operators directly into active feeds with minimal latency.
